title: DEAD CLIC: debit and credit
lines: | Expenses and losses | Income and gains
- D-E-A-D: Debit for Drawings, Expenses, Assets.
- C-L-I-C: Credit for Liabilities, Income, Capital.
- A decrease goes on the opposite side.
! Drawings are a debit but not an expense: they never enter profit and loss.

title: Golden rules
lines: | Personal (people, firms, banks) | Debit the receiver, credit the giver
| Real (assets) | Debit what comes in, credit what goes out
| Nominal (expenses, incomes) | Debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains
> Cash sale: Cash comes in (real, Dr); Sales is income (nominal, Cr).
! Outstanding Salaries is a representative personal account; Salaries itself is nominal.

title: Accounting equation
lines: - Closing capital = Opening capital + Profit + New capital − Drawings
- Profit = Closing capital − Opening capital + Drawings − New capital
! Paying a creditor lowers assets and liabilities; capital does not change. Paying an expense lowers assets and capital.

title: Concepts in one line
lines: | Business entity | Owner and business are separate
| Money measurement | Only money items recorded
| Matching | Expense in the year it helps earn revenue
| Prudence | Provide for losses, not gains
| Materiality | Ignore trivial items' strict treatment

title: Source documents
lines: | Debit note | Buyer | Goods returned to seller
| Credit note | Seller | Buyer owes less
| Receipt | Receiver of cash | Cash received
| Pay-in slip | Depositor | Money paid into bank

title: Subsidiary books
lines: | Purchases book | Credit purchases of goods for resale
| Sales book | Credit sales of goods
| Purchases returns book | Returns outwards (debit notes)
| Sales returns book | Returns inwards (credit notes)
| Cash book | All cash and bank items
| Journal proper | Fixed assets on credit, opening, adjusting and correcting entries
! Persons are posted one by one; the book total goes to the nominal account.

title: Discounts
lines: - Trade discount: off the list price, never entered in the ledger.
- Cash discount: for prompt payment, always recorded.
- Discount allowed (to customers): a loss, debit, profit and loss.
- Discount received (from suppliers): a gain, credit, profit and loss.
> List Rs 80,000, trade 20 %, cash 5 %: 64,000 − 3,200 = Rs 60,800 received.
! Apply discounts one after another; never add the rates.

title: Trial balance sides
lines: ! Closing stock is usually a note below the trial balance, not a balance in it.

title: Errors the trial balance misses
lines: - O: Original entry (wrong amount in the prime book)
! One-sided errors, wrong sides and casting errors do make it disagree; their difference goes to suspense.

title: Final accounts formulas
lines: - Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Returns outwards + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
- Gross profit = Net sales − Cost of goods sold
- Net profit = Gross profit + Other income − Expenses
- Working capital = Current assets − Current liabilities
! Carriage inwards: trading account. Carriage outwards: profit and loss.

title: Adjustment effects
lines: | Outstanding expense | Add to expense | Current liability
| Prepaid expense | Deduct from expense | Current asset
| Accrued income | Add to income | Current asset
| Income in advance | Deduct from income | Current liability
| Bad debts | Expense | Deduct from debtors
| Provision increase | Expense (increase only) | Deduct from debtors
| Closing stock | Credit trading | Current asset

title: Capital or revenue?
lines: - Capital expenditure: buying or improving a fixed asset, plus carriage, installation and legal costs to bring it into use.
- Revenue expenditure: repairs, repainting, fuel, wages, rent, running insurance.
- Capital receipt: sale of a fixed asset, loan, new capital.
- Revenue receipt: sales, commission, interest, rent received.
! Capital treated as revenue: profit and assets both understated.

title: Depreciation methods
lines: | Straight-line | (Cost − Residual) ÷ Life, same yearly | Falls evenly, can reach residual or nil
| Reducing balance | Fixed % of book value, falls yearly | Never reaches nil
- Profit or loss on sale = Proceeds − (Cost − Accumulated depreciation)

title: Bank reconciliation
lines: | From cash book (Dr) to bank statement | Action
- First update the cash book for charges, interest, direct credits and dishonoured cheques.
- From the bank statement back to the cash book: reverse each sign.
! A positive balance is a debit in the cash book but a credit on the bank statement.

title: Partnership without a deed
lines: Partnership Act, 1932 rules when nothing is agreed:
| Interest on partner's loan | 6 % a year

title: Bills of exchange
lines: - Drawer: creditor who writes the bill. Drawee: debtor who accepts it.
- Promissory note: a promise made by the debtor (maker).
- Due date = date + period + 3 days of grace.
- Discount on discounting = Amount × Rate × Months/12.
| Drawer | Bills Receivable Dr, Debtor Cr
| Drawee | Creditor Dr, Bills Payable Cr
! On dishonour, charge the debtor the bill amount plus noting charges.

title: Prokaryote vs eukaryote
lines: | Nucleus | none; DNA in nucleoid | membrane-bound nucleus
| DNA | circular, no histones; plasmids | linear, with histones
| Wall | peptidoglycan | plants cellulose; fungi chitin; animals none
| Organelles | no mitochondria, ER, Golgi | present
| Division | binary fission | mitosis and meiosis
! Mitochondria and chloroplasts have 70S ribosomes and circular DNA, like bacteria.

title: Organelles and their jobs
lines: | Smooth ER | lipids and steroids; detox in liver
| Golgi | modifies, packages, secretes; makes lysosomes
| Mitochondrion | aerobic respiration (Krebs in matrix, ETC on cristae)
| Chloroplast | photosynthesis (light stage in grana, Calvin cycle in stroma)
Secretory route: RER → vesicle → Golgi → secretory vesicle → cell membrane.

title: Carbohydrates at a glance
lines: | Maltose | glucose + glucose | from starch digestion
| Sucrose | glucose + fructose | non-reducing; moves in phloem
| Starch | α-glucose | plant store; iodine → blue-black
| Glycogen | α-glucose, highly branched | animal store: liver and muscle
| Cellulose | β-glucose, unbranched | plant cell wall
| Chitin | modified glucose (with nitrogen) | insect skeleton, fungal wall
! Glucose and fructose are both C₆H₁₂O₆: isomers. Humans cannot digest cellulose.

title: Four levels of protein structure
lines: | Level | What it is | Held by
| Primary | amino acid sequence | peptide bonds
| Secondary | α-helix or β-pleated sheet | hydrogen bonds
| Tertiary | 3-D folding of one chain | disulphide, ionic, hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic forces
| Quaternary | two or more chains | same as tertiary; e.g. haemoglobin 2α + 2β
- n amino acids in one chain → n − 1 peptide bonds, n − 1 water molecules lost.
! Denaturing (heat, wrong pH) destroys the 3-D shape but not the primary sequence.

title: DNA numbers
lines: - Watson and Crick, 1953 (X-ray data from Franklin and Wilkins).
- A = T (2 hydrogen bonds); G ≡ C (3 hydrogen bonds).
- Strands antiparallel; 10 base pairs per turn; 3.4 nm per turn.
! RNA has ribose and uracil; Chargaff's rule does not apply to single-stranded RNA.

title: Enzymes: how they work
lines: - Biological catalysts, mostly proteins; lower activation energy; not used up.
- Lock and key: Fischer. Induced fit: Koshland.
- Rate rises with temperature to an optimum (about 37 °C in humans), then falls as the enzyme denatures.
- More substrate: rate levels off when all active sites are full.
| Prosthetic group | organic, tightly bound | haem
| Coenzyme | organic, loosely bound | NAD⁺, FAD
Optimum pH: pepsin about 2, salivary amylase 6.8, pancreatic lipase about 9.

title: Enzyme inhibitors
lines: | Type | Binds to | More substrate helps?
| Competitive | active site; looks like substrate | yes
| Non-competitive | another site; changes shape | no
| Irreversible | enzyme, by strong bonds | no; enzyme lost
Feedback inhibition: the end product switches off the first enzyme of its own pathway.
! Strong inhibition at low substrate that vanishes at high substrate = competitive.

title: Respiration: where and how much
lines: | Glycolysis | cytoplasm | 2 pyruvate, net 2 ATP, 2 NADH
| Link reaction | matrix | 2 acetyl CoA, 2 CO₂, 2 NADH
| Krebs cycle (2 turns) | matrix | 4 CO₂, 6 NADH, 2 FADH₂, 2 ATP
| ETC | inner membrane (cristae) | most ATP; O₂ + H⁺ → H₂O
- Aerobic total: about 36-38 ATP per glucose.
- No O₂: muscle → lactic acid; yeast → ethanol + CO₂; net 2 ATP.
! O₂ is the final electron acceptor. Cyanide blocks the chain.

title: Photosynthesis in two stages
lines: | Light-dependent | thylakoids (grana) | light, H₂O, ADP, NADP⁺ | O₂, ATP, NADPH
| Calvin cycle | stroma | CO₂, ATP, NADPH | sugar (via PGAL)
- Rubisco fixes CO₂ onto RuBP (5C) → 2 PGA (3C).
- Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light best; green is reflected.
! The O₂ released comes from water (photolysis), not from CO₂.

title: Classification and the kingdoms
lines: Ranks, largest to smallest: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.
Mnemonic: King Philip Came Over For Good Soup (Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species).
- Binomial name (Linnaeus): Genus capital, species small, in italics: Homo sapiens.
! Viruses are in no kingdom: acellular, DNA or RNA, reproduce only in a host cell.

title: Plant groups and monocot vs dicot
lines: | Angiosperms | yes | in fruit | wheat, mango
| Flower parts | threes | fours or fives
! Mosses: gametophyte dominant and need water for fertilisation. Ferns onwards: sporophyte dominant.

title: Animal phyla with examples
lines: | Arthropoda | jointed legs, chitin | insects, spiders, crabs
| Mollusca | soft body, shell | snail, octopus
| Echinodermata | spiny skin, tube feet | starfish
Heart chambers: fish 2, amphibians 3, reptiles 3 (crocodile 4), birds 4, mammals 4.

title: Ecology essentials
lines: - Producers → primary → secondary → tertiary consumers; decomposers recycle.
- Nitrogen: fixation (Rhizobium), nitrification (Nitrosomonas then Nitrobacter), denitrification (back to N₂).
- Acid rain: SO₂ and NOₓ. Ozone damage: CFCs. Greenhouse: CO₂, methane.

title: Digestive enzymes
lines: | Enzyme | Made by | Acts on → gives
| Salivary amylase | salivary glands | starch → maltose
| Pancreatic lipase | pancreas | fat → fatty acids + glycerol
| Maltase, sucrase, lactase | small intestine wall | disaccharides → monosaccharides
| Peptidases | small intestine wall | peptides → amino acids
! HCl activates pepsinogen; enterokinase activates trypsinogen. Bile has no enzyme: it emulsifies fat.

title: Heart and vessels
lines: - Right side: right atrium → tricuspid → right ventricle → pulmonary artery.
- Left side: pulmonary veins → left atrium → bicuspid (mitral) → left ventricle → aorta.
- Impulse: SA node → AV node → bundle of His → Purkinje fibres.
- Lubb = AV valves close; dub = semilunar valves close.
- At 75 beats/min: cycle 0.8 s = atrial systole 0.1 + ventricular systole 0.3 + diastole 0.4.
! Pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood; pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.

title: Breathing, gases and lung volumes
lines: - Breathing in: diaphragm contracts and flattens; external intercostals lift ribs.
- O₂: about 97 % as oxyhaemoglobin. CO₂: about 70 % as bicarbonate.
- CO binds haemoglobin about 200 times more strongly than O₂.
- Vital capacity = TV + IRV + ERV. Total lung capacity = VC + RV.
! Residual volume is not part of vital capacity. Breathing centre: medulla, driven mainly by CO₂.

title: Down the nephron
lines: - Glomerulus → Bowman's capsule: ultrafiltration (no cells, no plasma proteins).
- Proximal tubule: reabsorbs all glucose and amino acids, most water and salts.
- Loop of Henle: concentrates the medulla so water can be drawn out.
- Distal tubule: aldosterone → more Na⁺ reabsorbed.
- Collecting duct: ADH → more water reabsorbed, less urine.
! Urea is made in the liver; the kidney only removes it. Glucose in urine suggests diabetes mellitus; protein suggests glomerular damage.

title: Nerves and the brain
lines: - Resting potential about −70 mV. Depolarisation: Na⁺ in. Repolarisation: K⁺ out.
- All-or-none; myelinated fibres conduct fastest (node to node).
- Synapse: acetylcholine crosses the gap; one-way transmission.
- Reflex arc: receptor → sensory → relay → motor neuron → effector.
! Myopia: image in front of retina, concave lens. Hypermetropia: behind retina, convex lens.

title: Hormones to know
lines: | Anterior pituitary | GH, TSH, FSH, LH | growth; controls other glands
| Posterior pituitary | ADH, oxytocin | water reabsorption; labour
| Pancreas | insulin / glucagon | lowers / raises blood glucose
| Adrenal medulla | adrenaline | fight or flight
| Ovaries | oestrogen, progesterone | female characters; uterus lining
! Too little iodine → goitre. Too little insulin → diabetes mellitus. Too little ADH → diabetes insipidus.

title: Immunity
lines: Antibody classes: GAMED (IgG, IgA, IgM, IgE, IgD).
| IgG | most abundant; crosses the placenta
- B cells → plasma cells → antibodies (humoral). T cells mature in the thymus (cell-mediated).
| Passive | mother's milk, placenta | injected antibodies
! HIV destroys helper T cells, so both arms of immunity fail.

title: Reproduction
lines: Sperm path, SEVEN UP: Seminiferous tubules, Epididymis, Vas deferens, Ejaculatory duct, (Nothing), Urethra, Penis.
| 6-13 | follicle grows; lining rebuilds | FSH → oestrogen rises
| 15-28 | corpus luteum; lining ready | progesterone high
- Fertilisation happens in the oviduct (Fallopian tube).
- 1 primary spermatocyte → 4 sperm; 1 primary oocyte → 1 egg + polar bodies.

title: Mendel's ratios and gametes
lines: - Product rule: chance of rryy from RrYy × RrYy = ¼ × ¼ = 1/16.
! Of the tall F₂ plants from Tt × Tt, 2/3 are heterozygous.

title: Sex linkage, blood groups and syndromes
lines: - X-linked recessive (haemophilia, colour blindness): more common in males.
- Father never passes an X-linked allele to his son.
- Carrier mother × normal father: ½ sons affected, ½ daughters carriers.

title: Genetic code and biotechnology
lines: - 64 codons, 20 amino acids: triplet, degenerate, nearly universal.
- Start: AUG. Stop: UAA, UAG, UGA.
- Transcription: DNA → mRNA (nucleus). Translation: mRNA → protein (ribosome).
| Restriction enzyme | cuts DNA at a set sequence
| Plasmid | vector that carries a gene into bacteria
| PCR (Taq polymerase) | copies DNA: 2ⁿ copies after n cycles
| Gel electrophoresis | sorts DNA by size; DNA fingerprinting
- Products: human insulin from E. coli; Bt cotton; Dolly the sheep (1996, cloned from an adult cell).

title: Evolution
lines: | Idea | use and disuse; acquired characters inherited | natural selection of inherited variation
| Book | Philosophie Zoologique (1809) | On the Origin of Species (1859)
- Homologous organs: same structure, different job (human arm, bat wing, whale flipper).
- Analogous organs: same job, different origin (bird and insect wings).
- Miller and Urey (1953): sparks in CH₄, NH₃, H₂, H₂O → amino acids.
! Herbert Spencer, not Darwin, coined "survival of the fittest".

title: The mole at a glance
lines: | gas volume at STP | V ÷ 22.4 dm³
- Empirical formula: divide by atomic mass, then by the smallest result.
- Limiting reactant: smallest value of moles ÷ coefficient.
! Molecules or atoms? 9 g of water is 0.5 mol: 3.01 × 10²³ molecules but 9.03 × 10²³ atoms.

title: Gas laws
lines: | Dalton | P(total) = p₁ + p₂ + … | V, T
- PV = nRT; R = 0.0821 dm³ atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.
- Real gases are most ideal at low pressure and high temperature.
! H₂ diffuses 4 times as fast as O₂ (√(32/2) = 4).

title: Intermolecular forces and solids
lines: - Strength for similar sizes: London < dipole-dipole < hydrogen bond.
- Hydrogen bonds need H on F, O or N: water boils at 100 °C, H₂S is a gas.
- Boiling point: vapour pressure = external pressure.
| Ionic | NaCl | only molten or dissolved
| Covalent network | diamond, SiO₂ | no (graphite yes)
| Metallic | Cu | yes, as a solid
! Ice is less dense than water because hydrogen bonds hold its molecules in an open lattice.

title: Atomic particles and quantum numbers
lines: | Particle | Relative mass | Charge | Found through
- n shell; l = 0 to n − 1 (s, p, d, f); m = −l to +l; s = ±½.
- Shell holds 2n²; subshells s 2, p 6, d 10, f 14.

title: Filling orbitals
lines: - Pauli: at most 2 electrons per orbital, opposite spins.
- Hund: fill degenerate orbitals singly, spins parallel, before pairing.
! N (2p³) has 3 unpaired electrons, O (2p⁴) has 2.

title: VSEPR shapes
lines: | Bond pairs, lone pairs | Shape | Angle | Example
! Repulsion: lone-lone > lone-bond > bond-bond, so CH₄ > NH₃ > H₂O in bond angle.

title: Hybridisation and bond order
lines: - Single = σ; double = σ + π; triple = σ + 2π. Ethene 5σ 1π; ethyne 3σ 2π.
- Bond order = (bonding − antibonding electrons) ÷ 2: N₂ 3, O₂ 2, He₂ 0.
- O₂ is paramagnetic (2 unpaired electrons), explained only by MO theory.
! Symmetrical CO₂, BF₃ and CCl₄ have zero dipole moment despite polar bonds.

title: Thermochemistry
lines: - Exothermic ΔH < 0; endothermic ΔH > 0. Standard: 298 K, 1 atm.
| formation | zero for an element in its standard state
| neutralisation | about −57 kJ/mol (strong acid + strong base)
- Hess: ΔH is the same by any route; ΔH = ΣΔH(f, products) − ΣΔH(f, reactants).
- Reverse an equation: change the sign of ΔH.
- ΔG = ΔH − TΔS; spontaneous when ΔG < 0.

title: Equilibrium and Le Chatelier
lines: - Kc = [products]^coefficients ÷ [reactants]^coefficients; leave out pure solids and liquids.
- Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn (Δn = change in gas moles).
| raise pressure | to fewer gas moles | no
- Q < K: goes forward; Q > K: goes backward.

title: Acids, bases and pH
lines: | Arrhenius | gives H⁺ in water | gives OH⁻ in water
- NH₄Cl solution is acidic; CH₃COONa is basic; NaCl is neutral.
- Indicators: methyl orange for strong acid + weak base; phenolphthalein for weak acid + strong base.
! Diluting a strong acid tenfold raises pH by 1, but never above 7.

title: Reaction kinetics
lines: - Rate = k[A]ˣ[B]ʸ; order = x + y, found by experiment.
- Arrhenius k = Ae^(−Ea/RT); a 10 K rise roughly doubles the rate near room temperature.
! A catalyst lowers Ea for both directions; ΔH and K do not change.

title: Oxidation numbers: OIL RIG
lines: Mnemonic "OIL RIG": Oxidation Is Loss of electrons, Reduction Is Gain.
- Elements 0; F always −1; sum = charge on the species.
- Mn +7 in KMnO₄; Cr +6 in K₂Cr₂O₇; S +6 in H₂SO₄.
- The oxidising agent is reduced; the reducing agent is oxidised.
! Disproportionation: Cl₂ + cold NaOH gives Cl⁻ (−1) and OCl⁻ (+1).

title: Cells and electrolysis
lines: | Energy | chemical to electrical | electrical to chemical
- E°(cell) = E°(cathode) − E°(anode); Daniell cell 1.10 V.
- 1 F = 96,500 C per mole of electrons.
- 1 F deposits 108 g Ag, 31.75 g Cu, 9 g Al, or 11.2 dm³ H₂ at STP.
! Metals with more negative E° are stronger reducing agents and displace H₂ from acids.

title: Solutions and colligative properties
lines: - Molarity: mol per dm³ of solution. Molality: mol per kg of solvent.
- Mole fraction: moles of component ÷ total moles.
- Raoult: vapour pressure ∝ mole fraction of the solvent.
- ΔT(b) = Kb m (water 0.52); ΔT(f) = Kf m (water 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹).
- Electrolytes: multiply by particles per formula (NaCl 2, CaCl₂ 3).
! Molality does not change with temperature; molarity does.

title: Periodic trends
lines: | Property | Across a period | Down a group
- IE exceptions: Be > B, Mg > Al; N > O, P > S.
- Isoelectronic: O²⁻ > F⁻ > Na⁺ > Mg²⁺ > Al³⁺.
- Period 3 oxides: basic (Na, Mg), amphoteric (Al), acidic (Si to Cl).
! Electronegativity: F > O > N ≈ Cl > C > H.

title: Groups 1 and 2
lines: - Group 2 down: hydroxides more soluble, sulphates less soluble (BaSO₄ insoluble).
- Diagonal pairs: Li with Mg, Be with Al.
! Plaster of Paris CaSO₄·½H₂O; gypsum CaSO₄·2H₂O.

title: Halogens and noble gases
lines: | Halogen | State at room temperature | AgX precipitate
| F₂ | pale yellow gas | none (AgF soluble)
- Oxidising power F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.
- Acid strength HI > HBr > HCl > HF.
- Xenon forms XeF₂ (linear), XeF₄ (square planar), XeF₆.
! The strongest X–X bond is Cl–Cl, not F–F.

title: Transition elements
lines: - Variable oxidation states, coloured ions, paramagnetism, complexes, catalysis.
- MnO₄⁻ (purple) → Mn²⁺ gains 5 e⁻; Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) → Cr³⁺ (green) gains 6 e⁻.

title: Industrial processes
lines: | Ostwald | HNO₃ | Pt-Rh gauze | NH₃ oxidised to NO
| Solvay | Na₂CO₃ | none | NaCl, NH₃, CO₂, limestone
| Hydrogenation | vanaspati ghee | nickel | oil + H₂
- Urea CO(NH₂)₂: 46.7 % N; ammonium nitrate 35 %; ammonium sulphate 21.2 %.
! SO₃ is absorbed in 98 % H₂SO₄ (oleum), not in water.

title: Functional groups and names
lines: - Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkenes CₙH₂ₙ, alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
! Isomer counts: C₄H₁₀ 2, C₅H₁₂ 3, C₄H₁₀O 4 alcohols + 3 ethers.

title: Organic reaction types
lines: - Markovnikov: H adds to the carbon with more H.
- Aqueous KOH substitutes; alcoholic KOH eliminates.

title: Tests for organic compounds
lines: | Bromine water | C=C, phenol | decolourised (white ppt with phenol)
| Baeyer's (cold KMnO₄) | C=C | purple colour lost
| Iodoform | CH₃CO– or CH₃CH(OH)– | yellow precipitate
! Lucas test: 3° alcohol cloudy at once, 2° in minutes, 1° not at room temperature.

title: Polymers
lines: ! Condensation polymers lose water at each link; addition polymers lose nothing.

title: Biomolecules
lines: - Glucose: aldohexose; fructose: ketohexose; both C₆H₁₂O₆.
- Sucrose = glucose + fructose, non-reducing; maltose and lactose reduce Fehling's.
- Starch and cellulose: polymers of glucose.
- Proteins: amino acids joined by peptide bonds –CO–NH–; n amino acids, n − 1 bonds.
- Fats: triglycerides; alkaline hydrolysis is saponification (soap).
- DNA: A–T and G–C pairs; RNA uses uracil instead of thymine.
- Enzymes are proteins; heat denatures them.
! Glycine is the only common amino acid without a chiral carbon.

title: Documents of home trade
lines: | pro forma invoice | seller | no payment demanded
| debit note | seller | buyer owes more
| credit note | seller | buyer owes less
| statement of account | seller | periodic balance
! E. & O.E. = errors and omissions excepted.

title: Documents of foreign trade
lines: | indent | import order through an agent
| mate's receipt | given on loading; exchanged for bill of lading
| bill of lading | receipt, contract and document of title (sea)
| charter party | hiring a whole ship
| letter of credit | bank undertakes to pay exporter
| certificate of origin | where goods were made
| bill of entry / shipping bill | customs: importer / exporter

title: Price terms
lines: | C.I.F. | cost, insurance, freight to destination port
! Discounts: trade discount first, then cash discount on the reduced amount.

title: Middlemen
lines: - Broker: arranges deals, never holds goods.
- Factor: holds goods, may sell in own name.
- Del credere agent: guarantees buyers will pay, for extra commission.
- Auctioneer: sells to the highest bidder.

title: Forms of business compared
lines: | owners | one | two or more | shareholders
| liability | unlimited | unlimited, joint and several | limited
| continuity | ends with owner | ends on dissolution | perpetual succession
| key document | none | partnership deed | memorandum and articles

title: Kinds of partners
lines: ! A minor: benefits only, with all partners' consent; liability limited to his share.

title: Company documents and doctrines
lines: - Memorandum: charter; objects; relations with outsiders.
- Certificate of incorporation: the company's birth.
- Constructive notice: outsiders presumed to know the documents.
- Indoor management: outsiders may assume internal rules were followed.

title: Shares and debentures
lines: | ordinary share | owner, votes | varying dividend
| preference share | owner, priority | fixed dividend, paid first
| debenture | creditor | fixed interest, even in a loss year
- Bonus shares: free from reserves. Right shares: offered first to members, paid for.
- Paid-up capital = called-up capital − calls in arrears.
! Special resolution: three-fourths of votes cast; ordinary: simple majority.

title: Cooperatives and public enterprises
lines: - Cooperative: service motive, one member one vote, elected committee, surplus by patronage.
- Departmental undertaking: run by a ministry, budget-financed.
- Statutory corporation: created by a special Act, separate legal person.
- Government company: state holds majority shares, registered as a company.

title: Negotiable instruments
lines: | bill of exchange | order | drawer, drawee, payee
| cheque | order on a banker, on demand | drawer, bank, payee
! Days of grace: 3 days for bills and notes not payable on demand; none for cheques.

title: Kinds of crossing
lines: | general (two lines) | pay only through a bank account
| special (bank named) | pay only through that bank
| Not Negotiable | no better title than the transferor's
| Account Payee | credit only to the payee's account
- Post-dated: future date. Stale: presented too late. Bearer: pay whoever presents it.

title: Endorsements
lines: - Blank: signature only; becomes payable to bearer.
- Restrictive: "Pay Ali only"; stops further negotiation.
- Sans recourse: endorser excludes his own liability.
- Holder in due course: for value, in good faith, before maturity.

title: Principles of insurance
lines: Mnemonic "I Insure Under Proper Care, Sir":
- C: Contribution (double insurance, shared by ratio of sums insured)
- S: Subrogation (insurer takes over the insured's rights)

title: Islamic modes of finance
lines: | mudarabah | capital from one, skill from other
| musharakah | all give capital; share profit and loss
| salam | price in advance, goods later

title: Transport and warehouses
lines: | rail | heavy goods, long land routes
- Liners: fixed routes. Tramps: no fixed route.
- Bonded warehouse: imports before duty paid. Warehouse warrant: document of title.

title: Stock exchange terms
lines: | stag | buys new issues to sell at a premium
| lame duck | bear unable to meet commitments
! Pakistan Stock Exchange: formed 2016 by merging Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad exchanges; regulated by SECP.

title: Marketing and letters
lines: - Four Ps: product, price, place, promotion.
- Life cycle: introduction, growth, maturity, decline.
- Filing: alphabetical, numerical (needs index), geographical, subject, chronological.
- "Dear Sir" → Yours faithfully; "Dear Mr Raza" → Yours sincerely.
- Agenda before a meeting; minutes after it.

title: Processing cycle and software
lines: | Storage | hard disk, SSD, USB flash, DVD
- Data = raw facts; information = processed, meaningful data.
- System software: OS, utilities (antivirus, defragmenter, backup), translators.
- Application software: word processor, spreadsheet, browser.
! A touchscreen is both an input and an output device.

title: CPU, registers and buses
lines: | Control unit | fetches, decodes, sends control signals
| PC | address of the next instruction
| MAR / MDR | memory address / data being moved
| Address bus | CPU → memory, one way
| Control bus | read, write, clock signals
! n-bit address bus → 2ⁿ locations: 16 bits → 65,536; 20 bits → 1,048,576.

title: Memory types
lines: | ROM | no | boot program; read only
| Cache | yes | fast SRAM between CPU and RAM
| Secondary | no | hard disk, SSD, CD/DVD, tape
- Fastest → slowest: registers → cache → RAM → secondary storage.
- PROM: write once. EPROM: erased by UV light. EEPROM and flash: erased electrically.
- Magnetic: hard disk, tape. Optical: CD, DVD, Blu-ray. Solid state: SSD, USB flash.
! Tape is sequential access only; disks allow direct access.

title: Units of data
lines: - Order: bit < nibble < byte < KB < MB < GB < TB < PB.
! Some sources use 1 KB = 1,000 bytes (SI units); HSSC questions normally use 1,024.

title: Number conversions
lines: - Decimal → binary: divide by 2; read remainders bottom to top.
- Binary → octal: groups of 3 from the right. Binary → hex: groups of 4.

title: Two's complement and character codes
lines: - Negative number: invert all bits of the positive number, then add 1.
- One's complement: just invert the bits.
| Unicode | 16 or more | nearly all languages, including Urdu

title: Translators and errors
lines: | Assembler | assembly → machine code | instruction by instruction
| Compiler | high-level → machine code | whole program at once; lists all errors
| Interpreter | high-level → runs directly | one line at a time; stops at first error
| Runtime | while running | division by zero
! Logic errors are the hardest to find: there is no message, only a wrong answer.

title: Operating system
lines: | Process management | decides which program gets the CPU
| Memory management | gives and frees RAM
| File management | creates, copies, deletes files and folders
| Device management | controls hardware through drivers
| User interface | GUI or command line
- Real-time OS: responds at once (machine control). Multi-user: many users share one system.
- Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+S save.
! Deleted from hard disk → Recycle Bin (restorable). Deleted from a USB drive → usually gone for good.

title: Word processor and spreadsheet
lines: - Mail merge: one main document + data source → one copy per record.
- Find and Replace changes every match at once. Format Painter copies formatting only.
- Justify lines text up with both margins. A page break starts a new page.
> $A1 fixes the column; A$1 fixes the row.
- With B2:B4 = 10, 20, 30: SUM 60, AVERAGE 20, MAX 30, COUNT 3.

title: Network types and topologies
lines: - Client-server: central server. Peer-to-peer: all equal.
| Topology | Layout | If one part fails
| Bus | one backbone cable | backbone break stops all
| Star | all to a central switch | centre fails → all fail
| Ring | closed loop | one break can stop all
| Mesh | every node to every other | most reliable, most cable
| Tree | stars in a hierarchy | a branch is cut off
! Full mesh of n nodes needs n(n − 1) ÷ 2 links: 6 nodes → 15.

title: The 7 OSI layers
lines: Mnemonic, layer 1 to 7: Please Do Not Throw Samosas, Pakoras Away.
| 1 Physical | bits on the medium | hub, repeater
| 2 Data link | frames, MAC addresses | switch, bridge
| 5 Session | open and close a conversation | -
| 7 Application | user services | HTTP, FTP, SMTP, DNS
! TCP is reliable and resends lost data; UDP is faster with no guarantee. TCP/IP model has 4 layers.

title: Network devices and addresses
lines: | Switch | sends to one port, by MAC address
| Router | joins networks, routes by IP address
| NIC | connects a computer; holds the MAC address

title: Protocols, ports and IP classes
lines: ! 127.x.x.x is the loopback address, used to test a computer's own network software.

title: Transmission modes and media
lines: | Half duplex | both ways, one at a time | walkie-talkie
| Full duplex | both ways at once | phone call
- Twisted pair: cheap, LANs. Coaxial: shielded, cable TV. Fibre optic: light, highest bandwidth, no electrical interference.
- Wireless: radio (Wi-Fi), microwave (line of sight), infrared (short range), satellite.
! Packet switching (internet) splits data into packets; circuit switching keeps one path for the whole call.

title: Malware and protection
lines: | Virus | attaches to a file; spreads when it runs
| Worm | spreads across networks by itself
| Trojan horse | looks useful, hides harm; does not copy itself
| Phishing | fake messages to steal passwords
- Antivirus removes malware; a firewall filters traffic by rules.
- Encryption: plaintext → ciphertext with a key. Symmetric: one key. Public-key: public key locks, private key unlocks.

title: Ethics and software licences
lines: | Copyright | protects original work (code, books, music)
| Piracy | copying software without a licence
| Plagiarism | passing off others' work as your own
| Hacking | entering a system without permission
| Freeware | free to use; code not open
| Open source | code free to read and change
| Proprietary | owned and licensed by a company
! Typing whole sentences in capitals is poor netiquette: it reads as shouting.

title: C operators
lines: - x++ uses then increases; ++x increases then uses.
! = assigns; == compares. if (x = 5) is always true.

title: printf, scanf and cout
lines: - Escapes: \n new line, \t tab, \\ backslash, \0 null character.
- scanf("%d", &n); needs the & (address). C++: cin >> n; cout << n << endl;
! A char array name for %s needs no & in scanf.

title: if and switch
lines: - if (x == 5) compares; if (x = 5) assigns and is always true.
- else pairs with the nearest unmatched if.
- big = (a > b) ? a : b; is a short if-else.
- switch case labels must be int or char constants.
> switch (n) { case 1: printf("one "); case 2: printf("two "); case 3: printf("three "); }
> Output: two three (no break, so it falls through)
! Put break; at the end of each case unless fall-through is wanted.

title: Tracing loops
lines: - for (i = a; i <= b; i++) runs b − a + 1 times; with i < b it runs b − a times.
- while tests first (may run 0 times); do-while tests last (runs at least once).
- continue skips to the next round; break leaves the loop.
! for (i = 0; i < 3; i++); has an empty body: the next line runs once, with i = 3.

title: Arrays, strings and functions
lines: - Arguments are passed by value: the function changes only its copy.
- A recursive function calls itself and needs a base case.
! &x is the address of x; if p = &x, then *p is x itself.

title: Flowchart symbols
lines: - An algorithm is a finite list of clear, ordered steps.
- Pseudocode writes the steps in plain structured English.
! Reading marks is input (parallelogram); calculating the average is a process (rectangle).

title: Database keys
lines: | Super key | any field set that identifies each row
| Candidate key | a minimal super key
| Primary key | the chosen candidate key; unique, not NULL
| Alternate key | a candidate key not chosen
| Composite key | two or more fields together
| Foreign key | matches another table's primary key
> Student(RollNo, CNIC, Name): RollNo and CNIC are candidate keys; RollNo is primary, CNIC alternate.
! Name is not a key: two students can share a name. A foreign key value may repeat.

title: Normal forms and integrity
lines: | 2NF | 1NF + no partial dependency on part of a composite key
- Entity integrity: primary key never NULL.
- Referential integrity: each foreign key matches an existing primary key.
- 1:M relationship: the foreign key goes in the "many" table. M:N needs a linking table.
! A 1NF table whose primary key is a single field is already in 2NF.

title: SQL cheat sheet
lines: > SELECT Name FROM Student WHERE City = 'Lahore' ORDER BY Marks DESC;
- Aggregates: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX. WHERE filters rows; HAVING filters groups.
- BETWEEN includes both ends. IS NULL, not = NULL.
- LIKE: % any number of characters, _ exactly one. LIKE 'S%' = starts with S.
! DELETE removes rows; DROP TABLE removes the whole table and its structure.

title: Definitions of economics
lines: | Lionel Robbins | scarce means with alternative uses
- Opportunity cost: the next best alternative given up.
- PPC bowed outward: rising opportunity cost. Inside: idle resources. Outside: unattainable.

title: Shift or movement?
lines: | the good's own price | movement along the curve
| income, tastes, related prices, expectations | demand curve shifts
| costs, technology, taxes, subsidies | supply curve shifts
- Demand up: price up, quantity up.
- Supply up: price down, quantity up.
! Ceiling below equilibrium: shortage. Floor above equilibrium: surplus.

title: Elasticity formulas
lines: - Midpoint method: divide each change by the average of the old and new values.
! Quantity change always goes on top.

title: Reading elasticity signs
lines: | PED above 1 | elastic: price cut raises revenue
| PED below 1 | inelastic: price rise raises revenue
| PED = 1 | unitary: revenue unchanged, and at its maximum
- Horizontal curve: perfectly elastic. Vertical curve: perfectly inelastic (zero).

title: Utility and consumer equilibrium
lines: - MU = change in TU from one more unit; MU falls (law of diminishing MU).
- Equi-marginal rule: MUx ÷ Px = MUy ÷ Py, all income spent.
- Consumer surplus = willing to pay − actually paid.
- Indifference curves: downward, convex (diminishing MRS), never cross.
- Equilibrium: budget line tangent to the highest indifference curve.

title: Factors and rewards: LLCE
lines: ! Entrepreneur bears uncertainty (Knight); interest rewards parting with liquidity (Keynes).

title: Product curves
lines: - AP = TP ÷ L. MP = ΔTP from one more worker.
- MP cuts AP at the maximum of AP.
- TP is at its maximum when MP = 0.
- Stage II (rational stage): from maximum AP to MP = 0.
- Returns to scale: all inputs change together (long run).
- Diminishing returns: one input varies, others fixed (short run).

title: Cost formulas
lines: - AVC = TVC ÷ Q; ATC = TC ÷ Q = AFC + AVC
- MC cuts AVC and ATC at their lowest points.
- Break-even Q = fixed cost ÷ (price − variable cost per unit)
! Total cost at zero output = total fixed cost.

title: Revenue and profit rules
lines: - TR = P × Q; AR = TR ÷ Q = P; MR = ΔTR from one more unit.
- Short-run shutdown: price below minimum AVC.
- Perfect competition: P = AR = MR; long run, normal profit only.
- Monopoly: MR below AR; higher price, lower output than competition.

title: Market forms
lines: ! Monopsony = one buyer. Cartel = firms agreeing on price or output.

title: National income chain
lines: - GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad
- NI (factor cost) = NNP − indirect taxes + subsidies
- Disposable income = personal income − direct taxes
! Leave out transfer payments, second-hand sales and intermediate goods.

title: Consumption and multiplier
lines: - C = a + bY: saving is zero at Y = a ÷ (1 − b)

title: Unemployment and inflation types
lines: - Demand-pull: too much money, too few goods. Cost-push: rising costs.

title: Money: four functions
lines: - Fisher: MV = PT, so P = MV ÷ T.
- Gresham's law: bad money drives out good.

title: Banks and monetary policy
lines: - Central bank: note issue, banker to government and banks, lender of last resort, controls credit.
! Buying securities expands money; selling contracts it.

title: Taxes and Smith's canons
lines: - Direct: cannot be shifted (income tax). Indirect: can be shifted (sales tax).
- Progressive: rate rises with income. Proportional: one rate. Regressive: hits the poor harder.
- Canons, mnemonic 'ECCE': Equality, Certainty, Convenience, Economy.
- Inelastic demand: buyers bear the tax. Elastic demand: sellers bear it.

title: Trade and exchange rates
lines: - Absolute advantage: Adam Smith. Comparative advantage (lower opportunity cost): Ricardo.
- Terms of trade = export price index ÷ import price index × 100
- Balance of trade: goods only. Current account: goods, services, income, remittances.
- Depreciation: exports cheaper abroad, imports dearer at home.
- Tariff: tax on imports. Quota: limit on quantity. Dumping: selling abroad below home price.
! More rupees per dollar means a weaker rupee.

title: Key terms
lines: - Integrity: doing right when no one is watching.
- Merit: selection on ability and performance.
- Nepotism: favouring relatives; favouritism: favouring friends.
- Plagiarism: passing off others' work as your own.

title: Equality and equity
lines: - Equity: each gets what they need for a fair chance.
> A ramp for wheelchair users is equity: it gives the same access, not the same treatment.
! Check which one the question describes.

title: Prejudice family
lines: | Stereotype | judging a group by a few
| Discrimination | unfair treatment for group membership
| Bigotry | intolerance of other views or groups

title: Rights and duties
lines: - My right is someone else's duty; others' rights are my duties.
- Citizens' duties: obey the law, pay taxes, vote, respect others' rights, protect public property.
- Sustainability: do not harm future generations' ability to meet their needs.
! Claiming rights while ignoring duties is a common wrong option.

title: Professional conduct
lines: - Conflict of interest: declare it and stand aside.
- Report wrongdoing through proper channels first.
- Public safety comes before loyalty to an employer.
! "Everyone does it" is never a reason.

title: Moral thinkers
lines: | Socrates | the examined life; knowledge leads to virtue
| Kant | duty; act on rules all could follow
| Bentham, Mill | greatest good of the greatest number

title: Results or duty?
lines: - Utilitarianism (Bentham, Mill) judges an act by its results.
- Kant's duty ethics judges the act and the intention.
> Kant: lying is wrong even if it brings a good result.
- Virtue ethics (Aristotle) asks what a good person would do.

title: Shared moral teachings
lines: - Nearly all teach the Golden Rule.

title: Buddhism in brief
lines: - Four Noble Truths: suffering exists, it has a cause (craving), it can end, the path ends it.
- Noble Eightfold Path includes right speech, right action and right livelihood.
- Taxila and Takht-i-Bahi in Pakistan were Buddhist centres.

title: Answering case questions
lines: - Is it fair to everyone affected?
- Is it lawful and through proper channels?
- Would I accept it if done to me?
! Reject kind-sounding options that cover up wrongdoing.

title: Functions: domain and inverse
lines: - (f∘g)(x) = f(g(x)): apply g first; usually f∘g ≠ g∘f.
- Inverse: swap x and y, solve for y. f(x) = 2x + 3 gives f⁻¹(x) = (x − 3)/2.
- Domain of f⁻¹ = range of f. Graph of f⁻¹ = mirror of f in y = x.

title: Logarithms and indices
lines: - aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ; aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ; (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ; a⁰ = 1; a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ.
- log(mn) = log m + log n; log(m/n) = log m − log n; log mⁿ = n log m.
- Change of base: logₐb = log b ÷ log a, so logₐb × log_b a = 1.
! log(m + n) is not log m + log n. Reject any answer that makes a log argument ≤ 0.

title: Quadratic equations
lines: - α + β = −b/a; αβ = c/a; new equation x² − (sum)x + product = 0.
| > 0, not a square | real, unequal, irrational
- Vertex of y = ax² + bx + c at x = −b/2a: minimum if a > 0.
! Remainder of p(x) ÷ (x − a) is p(a).

title: Complex numbers and roots of unity
lines: - i² = −1, i³ = −i, i⁴ = 1: divide the power by 4 and use the remainder.
- z = a + bi: conjugate a − bi; |z| = √(a² + b²); z z̄ = |z|².
- Cube roots of 1: 1, ω, ω², with ω = (−1 + i√3)/2.
- ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0, so 1 + ω = −ω².
- Real coefficients: complex roots come in conjugate pairs.

title: Sequences and series
lines: | Sum of n terms | (n/2)[2a + (n − 1)d] | a(1 − rⁿ)/(1 − r)
- Infinite GP: a/(1 − r), only if |r| < 1.
- HP: reciprocals in AP; harmonic mean 2ab/(a + b). A > G > H, G² = AH.
! Three terms in AP: a − d, a, a + d. In GP: a/r, a, ar.

title: Matrices and determinants
lines: - (m × n)(n × p) gives m × p; usually AB ≠ BA.
- Swap two rows: sign changes. Two equal rows: 0.
- Symmetric Aᵗ = A; skew-symmetric Aᵗ = −A (zero diagonal).

title: Permutations and combinations
lines: - n things with p alike, q alike: n!/(p! q!). LEVEL gives 30.
- Probability: P(not A) = 1 − P(A); P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).
! Arrange (order matters): P. Choose (order does not matter): C.

title: Binomial theorem
lines: - (a + b)ⁿ has n + 1 terms; Tᵣ₊₁ = ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ.
- Middle term: n even, T(n/2 + 1); n odd, two middle terms.
- Term free of x: set the power of x in Tᵣ₊₁ to zero.
- (1 + x)ⁿ = 1 + nx + n(n − 1)x²/2! + … (|x| < 1 if n is not a positive integer).

title: Standard trig values
lines: - π rad = 180°; 1 rad ≈ 57.3°; arc l = rθ; sector ½r²θ.

title: Quadrant signs and identities
lines: Mnemonic "All Students Take Coffee": All positive in quadrant I, Sin in II, Tan in III, Cos in IV.
- sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.
- 90° ± θ, 270° ± θ: sin ↔ cos, tan ↔ cot.
- Sign always from the quadrant of the original angle.

title: Compound and multiple angles
lines: - sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B.
- cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B.
- tan(A ± B) = (tan A ± tan B)/(1 ∓ tan A tan B).
- sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A = 2 tan A/(1 + tan²A).
- sin 3A = 3 sin A − 4 sin³A; cos 3A = 4 cos³A − 3 cos A.
! cos(A + B) has a minus sign in the middle.

title: Sum and product formulas
lines: | sin C + sin D | 2 sin((C + D)/2) cos((C − D)/2)
| sin C − sin D | 2 cos((C + D)/2) sin((C − D)/2)
| cos C + cos D | 2 cos((C + D)/2) cos((C − D)/2)
| cos C − cos D | −2 sin((C + D)/2) sin((C − D)/2)
- 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A − B).
- 2 cos A cos B = cos(A + B) + cos(A − B).
- 2 sin A sin B = cos(A − B) − cos(A + B).
! cos C − cos D carries a minus sign.

title: Periods and ranges
lines: - sin(ax + b), cos(ax + b): period 2π/|a|; tan(ax + b): π/|a|.
- a sin x + b cos x ranges from −√(a² + b²) to √(a² + b²).
- Even: cos, sec. Odd: sin, tan, cot, cosec.
! sin²x and |sin x| have period π, not 2π.

title: Inverse trig functions
lines: - sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2; tan⁻¹x + cot⁻¹x = π/2.
- tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹((x + y)/(1 − xy)) if xy < 1.

title: Trig equations
lines: - Factorise quadratics in sin θ or cos θ; reject values outside [−1, 1].
- Change mixed functions to one function first.
! Never cancel sin θ or cos θ from both sides: factorise, or solutions are lost.

title: Standard limits
lines: ! Rational function as x → ∞: equal top and bottom degrees give the ratio of leading coefficients.

title: Derivatives
lines: | sin x | cos x | aˣ | aˣ ln a
| sec x | sec x tan x | tan⁻¹x | 1/(1 + x²)
- Product (uv)′ = u′v + uv′; quotient (vu′ − uv′)/v²; chain dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx).
! Every "co" function (cos, cot, cosec, cos⁻¹) gets a minus sign.

title: Applications of derivatives
lines: - Tangent slope m = f′(a); normal slope −1/m.
- Stationary point f′ = 0: f″ < 0 maximum, f″ > 0 minimum.
- Velocity v = ds/dt; acceleration a = dv/dt.
- Small change δy ≈ f′(x)δx; % error in xⁿ ≈ n × % error in x.
- Rectangle of fixed perimeter has greatest area when it is a square.
! Horizontal tangent: dy/dx = 0. Vertical tangent: dx/dy = 0.

title: Standard integrals
lines: ! Add + C. Check by differentiating the answer.

title: Integration methods
lines: - By parts ∫ u dv = uv − ∫ v du.
Mnemonic ILATE for choosing u: Inverse trig, Logarithmic, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential (earliest letter first).
- ∫ x eˣ dx = eˣ(x − 1) + C; ∫ ln x dx = x ln x − x + C.
! ∫ 1/(1 + x²) dx is tan⁻¹x, not ln(1 + x²).

title: Definite integrals and area
lines: - ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a); swapping limits changes the sign.
- Odd f: integral from −a to a is 0. Even f: twice the integral from 0 to a.
- Volume about the x-axis: π ∫ y² dx.
! The integral of sin x from 0 to 2π is 0, but the area is 4: split at the zeros.

title: Straight lines
lines: - Distance √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²); midpoint ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2).
- Slope m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁); for ax + by + c = 0, m = −a/b.
- Forms: y = mx + c; y − y₁ = m(x − x₁); x/a + y/b = 1.
- Point to line: |ax₁ + by₁ + c| ÷ √(a² + b²).
- Triangle area ½|x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|; zero means collinear.
! A vertical line x = k has undefined slope, not zero.

title: Circles
lines: - (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²: centre (h, k), radius r.
- x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0: centre (−g, −f), r = √(g² + f² − c).
- Tangent to x² + y² = r² at (x₁, y₁): xx₁ + yy₁ = r².
- y = mx + c touches x² + y² = a² when c² = a²(1 + m²).
- A line touches a circle when its distance from the centre equals r.
! Halve the x and y coefficients, then change their signs to get the centre.

title: Conic sections
lines: | Conic | Equation | c and e | Foci
| Ellipse | x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 | c² = a² − b², e < 1 | (±c, 0)
| Hyperbola | x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 | c² = a² + b², e > 1 | (±c, 0)
- e = c/a for ellipse and hyperbola.
- Latus rectum: parabola 4a; ellipse and hyperbola 2b²/a.
- Hyperbola asymptotes y = ±(b/a)x; rectangular hyperbola e = √2.

! Two equal vectors at 120° have a resultant equal to either one; at 90° it is √2 times either.

title: Equations of motion and projectiles
lines: | s = ut + ½at² | final speed v
- Velocity-time graph: slope = acceleration, area = displacement.
- Projectile: time 2u sin θ/g, height u² sin²θ/2g, range u² sin 2θ/g; greatest range at 45°.
- Angles θ and 90° − θ give equal ranges (30° and 60°).
! Dropped from rest, distances in successive seconds go 1 : 3 : 5 : 7.
! At the top of the path the speed is u cos θ, not zero.

title: Momentum and collisions
lines: - Momentum p = mv (kg m/s = N s). Newton's second law: F = Δp/Δt.
- Impulse = FΔt = change in momentum = area under a force-time graph.
- No external force: total momentum is conserved (collisions, explosions, gun recoil).
| Bodies stick together | conserved | greatest loss
- Equal masses in a head-on elastic collision exchange velocities.
! A ball bouncing back with the same speed has Δp = 2mv.
! Action and reaction act on different bodies, so they never cancel.

title: Work, energy and power
lines: - Work W = Fd cos θ; zero when the force is at right angles to the motion.
- Kinetic energy = ½mv² = p²/2m; potential energy near the surface = mgh.
- Work-energy principle: net work = change in kinetic energy.
- Speed after falling h from rest: v = √(2gh), whatever the mass.
- Power P = W/t = Fv; 1 hp = 746 W.
! Efficiency = useful output ÷ input × 100 %, always below 100 %.

title: Circular motion and gravitation
lines: - Centripetal acceleration v²/r = rω²; force mv²/r towards the centre.
- Gravitation F = Gm₁m₂/r²; at the surface g = GM/R².
- Orbital speed √(GM/r) ≈ 7.9 km/s near the Earth; period T² ∝ r³.
- Escape speed √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s, independent of the body's mass.
- Geostationary orbit: period 24 h, above the equator, about 36,000 km up.
- Apparent weight in a lift: m(g + a) accelerating up, m(g − a) accelerating down, zero in free fall.
! Centripetal force does no work, so the speed stays constant.

title: Fluids
lines: - Pressure at depth h: P = P₀ + ρgh; gauge pressure ρgh.
- Archimedes: upthrust = weight of fluid displaced. Fraction submerged when floating = ρ(body)/ρ(fluid).
- Continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ (volume flow rate Av is constant).
- Bernoulli: P + ½ρv² + ρgh = constant; faster flow, lower pressure.
- Torricelli: speed from a hole at depth h is √(2gh).
- Stokes' law: drag = 6πηrv; terminal velocity ∝ r².

title: SHM: spring and pendulum
lines: - SHM condition: a = −ω²x. Speed v = ω√(x₀² − x²).
- Greatest speed ωx₀ at the mean position; greatest acceleration ω²x₀ at the extremes.
| Depends on | m, k | l, g
| On the Moon | unchanged | longer by √6
- Seconds pendulum: T = 2 s, l ≈ 1 m.

title: Stationary waves and beats
lines: - Wave equation v = fλ; frequency does not change between media.
- String: v = √(T/μ), μ = mass per metre.
| String fixed at both ends | v/2L | all
| Pipe open at both ends | v/2L | all
| Pipe closed at one end | v/4L | odd only
- Node to node = λ/2; node to next antinode = λ/4.
- Beat frequency = |f₁ − f₂|. Wax lowers a fork's frequency; filing raises it.
! First overtone: open pipe 2f, closed pipe 3f.

title: Sound and the Doppler effect
lines: - Speed in air ≈ 332 m/s at 0 °C, rising about 0.61 m/s per °C; v ∝ √T (kelvin).
- Laplace corrected Newton's 280 m/s by using adiabatic changes: v = √(γP/ρ).
- Pressure change at constant temperature does not alter v.
- Intensity level L = 10 log(I/I₀) dB, I₀ = 10⁻¹² W/m²; × 10 intensity adds 10 dB.
| Source (speed u) | f′ = fv/(v − u) | f′ = fv/(v + u)
| Observer (speed u) | f′ = f(v + u)/v | f′ = f(v − u)/v
! Pitch depends on frequency, loudness on intensity, quality on overtones.

title: Kinetic theory and gas processes
lines: | Process | Condition | First law Q = ΔU + W
- C(p) − C(v) = R; γ = 5/3 monatomic, 1.4 diatomic.
! Use kelvin: 27 °C to 927 °C is 300 K to 1,200 K, so v(rms) doubles.

title: Heat engines and entropy
lines: - Carnot (the best possible): η = 1 − T₂/T₁, temperatures in kelvin.
- Carnot cycle: two isothermal and two adiabatic steps.
- Second law: no engine converts all its heat into work; heat does not flow by itself from cold to hot.
- Entropy change ΔS = ΔQ/T; total entropy rises in every real process.
! 327 °C and 27 °C are 600 K and 300 K: η = 50 %, not 92 %.

title: Electrostatics and capacitors
lines: - Coulomb: F = kq₁q₂/r²; in a medium F/ε(r).
- Field E = F/q = kq/r² (N/C = V/m); parallel plates E = V/d.
- Potential V = kq/r (a scalar); work W = qV.
- Gauss: flux through a closed surface = q(enclosed)/ε₀.
- C = Q/V; parallel plates C = ε(r)ε₀A/d; energy ½CV².

title: Resistors and cells
lines: - R = ρL/A; series R₁ + R₂; parallel 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.
- Wire stretched to n times its length: R × n².
- Cell: I = E/(R + r); terminal p.d. V = E − Ir.
- Greatest power to the load when R = r.
- Wheatstone bridge balanced when P/Q = R/S.
! Bulbs in series: the lower-watt bulb has more resistance and glows brighter.

title: Resistor colour code
lines: Mnemonic "BB ROY of Great Britain has a Very Good Wife": the first letters give the colours for digits 0 to 9.
- Bands: first digit, second digit, multiplier (× 10ⁿ), tolerance (gold ±5 %, silver ±10 %).

title: Magnetic fields and forces
lines: - Force on a wire F = BIL sin θ; force on a charge F = qvB sin θ.
- Charge at right angles to B: circle of radius r = mv/qB.
- Long straight wire B = μ₀I/2πr; solenoid B = μ₀nI (n = turns per metre).
- Fleming's left-hand rule: First finger Field, seCond finger Current, thuMb Motion.
- Ammeter: galvanometer + small shunt in parallel. Voltmeter: + large resistance in series.
! The magnetic force on a moving charge does no work: speed stays constant.

title: Induction, transformers and AC
lines: - Faraday: ε = −N ΔΦ/Δt; moving rod ε = BLv. Lenz: the induced current opposes the change.
- Inductor energy ½LI²; generator peak EMF NBAω.
- Transformer: V(s)/V(p) = N(s)/N(p) = I(p)/I(s); AC only.
- V(rms) = V₀/√2; 220 V mains peaks near 311 V.
Mnemonic "ELI the ICE man": in an inductor (L) the voltage E leads the current I; in a capacitor (C) the current I leads E.
! Frequency doubled: X(L) doubles, X(C) halves.

title: Mirrors, lenses and refraction
lines: - Mirror f = R/2. Lens and mirror formula 1/f = 1/p + 1/q (real-is-positive); m = q/p.
- Convex lens and concave mirror: f positive. Concave lens: f negative.
- Power P = 1/f (f in metres), dioptre; lenses in contact P = P₁ + P₂.
- Snell: n = sin i / sin r = c/v; wavelength in the medium λ/n.
- Critical angle sin C = 1/n; total internal reflection only from denser to less dense.
- Telescope M = f(o)/f(e), length f(o) + f(e). Magnifier M = 1 + d/f, d = 25 cm.
! Object inside F of a convex lens: virtual, upright, magnified image.

title: Wave optics
lines: - Coherent sources: same frequency, constant phase difference.
- Bright fringe: path difference nλ; dark: (n + ½)λ.
- Grating d sin θ = nλ, d = 1/N; highest order = whole part of d/λ.
- Malus I = I₀ cos²θ; Brewster tan θ = n.
- Only transverse waves can be polarised.
! 5,000 lines per cm means d = 2 × 10⁻⁶ m.

title: Photons and matter waves
lines: - E = hf = hc/λ; photon momentum p = h/λ.
- Photoelectric: hf = φ + K(max), K(max) = eV₀, φ = hf₀.
- De Broglie λ = h/mv; uncertainty Δx Δp ≈ h.
- Pair production needs at least 1.02 MeV; Compton scattering lengthens the X-ray wavelength.
! Below the threshold frequency no electrons emerge, however bright the light.

title: Hydrogen atom and X-rays
lines: - rₙ = n² × 0.053 nm; angular momentum nh/2π.
Mnemonic "Lazy Boys Play Billiards Professionally": Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, Brackett, Pfund, ending on n = 1 to 5.
- Lyman ultraviolet, Balmer visible, the rest infrared.
- X-ray λ(min) = hc/eV: higher tube voltage, shorter λ(min).
- LASER: Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation; needs population inversion.

title: Radioactivity and the nucleus
lines: - Ionising α > β > γ; penetrating γ > β > α.
- Binding energy = Δm c²; 1 u ↔ 931 MeV; BE per nucleon peaks near iron.
- Moderator slows neutrons; control rods absorb them.
! α count from the change in A ÷ 4; then β count from the Z balance.

title: Electronics and logic gates
lines: - n-type: pentavalent donor (P, As); p-type: trivalent acceptor (B, Ga).
- Forward bias: p side to +; barrier about 0.7 V for Si, 0.3 V for Ge.
- Full-wave rectifier on 50 Hz gives 100 Hz ripple; half-wave gives 50 Hz.
- Transistor I(E) = I(B) + I(C); gain β = I(C)/I(B).
! NAND and NOR are universal: any gate can be built from either.

title: Fractions as percentages
lines: - x % of y = y % of x: 8 % of 25 = 25 % of 8 = 2

title: Divisibility rules
lines: | 11 | alternating digit sum is 0 or a multiple of 11
> 7,392: digit sum 21, so divisible by 3 but not 9.

title: Primes and HCF, LCM
lines: - 1 is not prime; 2 is the only even prime.
- HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.
- Repeating events coincide again after the LCM of their intervals.
- Largest number dividing a, b, c with the same remainder = HCF of the differences.

title: Index laws
lines: | a to the power m/n | 8 to the power 2/3 = 2² = 4
! A negative power gives a reciprocal, never a negative number.

title: Quadratic facts
lines: - b² − 4ac > 0: two real roots; = 0: equal roots; < 0: no real roots
- Equation with roots p, q: x² − (p + q)x + pq = 0
- (x − a)(x − b) < 0 between the roots; > 0 outside
! Never divide by x: factorise and keep x = 0.

title: Sequences

- Sum of the first n odd numbers = n²

title: Functions
lines: - f(g(x)): do g first, then f. Usually f(g(x)) ≠ g(f(x)).
- Domain: no zero denominators, nothing negative under √.
- Inverse: write y = f(x), make x the subject, swap x and y.
- f⁻¹(a) = b exactly when f(b) = a.

title: Angles and polygons
lines: - Straight line 180°; round a point 360°; triangle 180°
- Interior angles of an n-sided polygon: (n − 2) × 180°
- Exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°
- Each exterior angle of a regular n-gon: 360° ÷ n

lines: - Diagonal of a square of side a: a√2
- Height of an equilateral triangle of side a: (√3/2)a

lines: | trapezium | ½(sum of parallel sides) × height
! Scale lengths by k: areas by k², volumes by k³.

title: Speed, distance, time
lines: - km/h to m/s: × 5/18; m/s to km/h: × 18/5
- Average speed = total distance ÷ total time
- Same distance at u and v: average speed = 2uv/(u + v)
- Towards each other: add speeds; same direction: subtract
- Train passing a pole: its own length; a platform: train + platform
! 2.5 h = 2 h 30 min, not 2 h 50 min.

title: Work and rates
lines: - A in a days, B in b days: together they do 1/a + 1/b per day
- Workers × days = constant for a fixed job

title: Profit, loss and discount
lines: - Price after a discount of d % = marked price × (100 − d)/100
- Two discounts a % and b %: single discount = a + b − ab/100
- Rise r % then fall r %: net fall of r²/100 %
! Profit and loss percentages are on the cost price.

title: Simple and compound interest

- Six months is T = ½ year; 3 months is ¼

title: Averages and statistics
lines: - Mean = sum ÷ count, so sum = mean × count
- Median: middle of the sorted list (average the two middle values if even)
- Mode: most frequent; range: largest − smallest
- Probability = favourable ÷ total; P(not A) = 1 − P(A)

title: Time and calendar
lines: - 30 days: April, June, September, November; February 28 (29 in a leap year)
- Leap year: divisible by 4; century years only if divisible by 400
- Ordinary year moves a date on 1 weekday; a leap year 2
- n days later: move on n mod 7 weekdays

title: Cricket rates
lines: - Run rate = runs ÷ overs; 1 over = 6 balls
- Required rate = runs needed ÷ overs left
- Economy rate = runs conceded ÷ overs bowled

title: Mental maths shortcuts
lines: - Estimate first: round to one significant figure.

title: Graphs at a glance

! Unequal widths: bar height = f ÷ width.

title: Averages: formulas
lines: - G.M. = nth root of the product; log G.M. = Σlog x ÷ n
- A.M. > G.M. > H.M. for unequal positive values

title: Median and mode, grouped
lines: ! L is a class boundary, not a class limit.

title: Shape and the three averages
lines: | Positive skew (right tail) | mean > median > mode
| Negative skew (left tail) | mean < median < mode

title: Dispersion formulas
lines: - Range = xₘ − x₀; coefficient = (xₘ − x₀) ÷ (xₘ + x₀)
- C.V. = (σ ÷ x̄) × 100; lower C.V. = more consistent
- Normal curve: Q.D. ≈ ⅔σ, M.D. ≈ ⅘σ

title: Changing the data
lines: | Median, mode | change the same way
| S.D. | σ × size of a (sign dropped)
! Adding b moves the centre but never the spread.

title: Skewness and kurtosis
lines: - Pearson: Sk = (mean − mode) ÷ σ = 3(mean − median) ÷ σ
! Lepto = slender, platy = flat (like a plate).

title: Index numbers
lines: - Chain index = previous chain × link relative ÷ 100
! Laspeyres looks back to base-year quantities; Paasche uses the present.

title: Counting rules
lines: - ⁿPᵣ = n! ÷ (n − r)!: order matters (posts, arrangements)
- ⁿCᵣ = n! ÷ [r!(n − r)!]: order does not matter (committees)
- Letters with p alike: n! ÷ p!
! Ask: does swapping two people give a new result? Yes → P, no → C.

title: Laws of probability
lines: - P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)
- Bayes: P(B₁ | A) = P(B₁)P(A | B₁) ÷ ΣP(Bᵢ)P(A | Bᵢ)

- Poisson: P(X = r) = e⁻ᵐ mʳ ÷ r!

title: Sampling and testing
lines: - Samples: Nⁿ with replacement, ᴺCₙ without
- SE of mean = σ ÷ √n; SE of proportion = √(pq ÷ n)
- Type I: reject true H₀ (prob α). Type II: accept false H₀ (prob β)

- Time series components: STCI = Secular trend, Seasonal (within a year), Cyclical (several years), Irregular (random)

title: Analogy method
lines: - Make a precise sentence linking the stem pair.
- Test each option in the same sentence, in the same order.
- Two fit? Tighten the sentence and test again.
! Same topic is not same relationship.

lines: ! Reversed order: WHOLE : PART does not match PART : WHOLE.
! Degree must move the same way: mild to strong, or strong to mild.
! Prefer links that are always true (lung : breathe), not loose associations (rose : red).
- Match parts of speech: NOUN : VERB with noun : verb.

lines: - Opposite of the noun zenith (highest point): nadir.

title: Synonym and antonym method
lines: - Use the word in your own sentence.
- Predict a meaning (or its opposite) before reading options.
- Match strength and tone: colossal is stronger than big.
! In antonym items, one wrong option is usually a synonym.

title: Context clue signals
lines: | but, although, however, yet, despite | contrasts
| and, also, moreover | continues the idea
| because, so, therefore | follows from a cause
| such as, that is, a colon | is defined nearby
! Hardly, rarely and not reverse the meaning.

title: Tense rules for blanks
lines: | since, for (still true) | present perfect | has lived since 2019
| by next year | future perfect | will have finished
| yesterday, ago | simple past | left two days ago
| by the time (past) | past perfect | had left before we came

title: Conditionals
lines: | Real future | If + present, will + verb
| Unreal present | If + past, would + verb
| Unreal past | If + had + past participle, would have + past participle
> If he had studied, he would have passed.

title: Agreement rules
lines: - Each, every, either, neither take a singular verb: Each of the boys is here.
- Either/neither … or/nor: the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
- Collective nouns (team, committee) take a singular verb when the group acts as one unit: The team has won.
- "The number of" is singular; "a number of" is plural.

title: Verb patterns
lines: | Followed by -ing | Followed by to + verb
| enjoy, avoid, finish | want, decide, hope
| suggest, mind, deny | agree, refuse, plan
- After modals use the base verb: must go, can swim.
- Look forward to + -ing: look forward to meeting you.

title: Prepositions
lines: | prefer X to Y | prefer X than Y

title: Articles
lines: - a before a consonant sound: a university, a one-way road.
- an before a vowel sound: an hour, an honest man, an MBA.
- the for something already known or unique: the sun, the Indus.

title: Two-blank strategy
lines: - Start with the blank that has the clearer clue.
- Cross out options whose word fails there.
- Test the survivors in the other blank.
! One right word and one wrong word = wrong option.

title: Comprehension question types
lines: | Main idea | covers the whole passage
| Detail | find and match the line
| Inference | must follow from the text
| Tone | check opinion words; usually moderate
| Purpose | ask why the sentence is there

title: Eliminating options
lines: - Extreme words: always, never, only, completely.
- True in life but not stated in the passage.
- Uses passage words but reverses their meaning.
! The passage wins over your own opinion.
